h1Question: How Can Chinese Factories Get Listed on International B2B Platforms for Free?
blufSummary: Chinese manufacturers can create a free supplier profile on FactoryAuditB2B that international buyers can find in the supplier directory. The application and the basic profile are free. A free listing does not mean the factory has been independently verified, and it does not guarantee orders. Verification status is assigned by a human reviewer after documents are checked, and it is never sold.

zeroToleranceList: Submitting a business licence or ISO certificate that does not belong to your company

faqs.question: Does a free supplier profile guarantee orders from international buyers?
faqs.answer: No. A free profile makes your company discoverable in the supplier directory. It does not guarantee inquiries, orders or any particular commercial outcome. Buyers decide who to contact based on the information and evidence available on the profile.

faqs.question: Is a free listing the same as being verified?
faqs.answer: No. A profile starts as self-declared. A verification status is only assigned after a reviewer checks the information and documents you submitted. FactoryAuditB2B does not sell verification status, and it does not sell or issue certificates.

faqs.question: What information should I prepare before applying?
faqs.answer: Prepare your registered company name, business licence, the products you make, your industry, factory location, basic production capability, and any certificates you hold. Profiles with complete, consistent information are easier for buyers to evaluate.

faqs.question: My company may already be in the directory. Should I apply again?
faqs.answer: No. Search the supplier directory first. If your profile is already there, claim the existing profile instead of submitting a duplicate application. Claiming lets you maintain certificates, photos and self-assessment information yourself.

h1Question: How Can a Chinese Factory Get Discovered by International Buyers?
blufSummary: International buyers usually shortlist suppliers from what they can verify before contact: a clear company identity, an export-ready company profile, specific product descriptions, stated production capability, current certificates, and real factory photos. A supplier directory profile is useful only when these details are complete and consistent, because buyers compare them side by side before sending an inquiry.

faqs.question: Do international buyers prefer manufacturers over trading companies?
faqs.answer: Buyers work with both. What matters is that the company type is stated accurately. A trading company presented honestly can be useful for consolidating orders, while a factory should be able to show production equipment and records. Problems arise when the company type is misrepresented.

faqs.question: Why do factory photos matter on a supplier profile?
faqs.answer: Photos let a buyer confirm that production facilities exist and match the stated capability. They should be your own, current and consistent with the equipment and products described in the profile. Photos taken from another factory undermine trust once noticed.

faqs.question: How does a buyer know which claims on a profile are verified?
faqs.answer: Each profile shows an evidence level that reflects how information was confirmed, from self-declared through document reviewed to independently verified or factory audited. Buyers can use that level to decide which claims need further checking. An audit is a deeper on-site assessment than verification.

faqs.question: Will completing a profile bring inquiries automatically?
faqs.answer: No. A complete profile makes your company easier to evaluate and more likely to be shortlisted, but inquiries depend on buyer demand and fit. FactoryAuditB2B does not promise orders or a specific number of inquiries.

h1Question: How Do You Build a Professional Supplier Profile for a Chinese Factory?
blufSummary: A professional factory profile answers the questions a buyer has before making contact: who the company is, where and what it manufactures, its products and MOQ, production capacity, quality management, certificates, export markets and real factory photos. Each claim should match the documents on file, because the profile is shown to buyers together with an evidence level that reflects how the information was confirmed.

zeroToleranceList: A capacity figure with no equipment or production records behind it

faqs.question: What is the most common gap in a Chinese factory profile?
faqs.answer: Product descriptions are often too broad. A category label alone does not tell a buyer what you make. Specific product names, materials and models, together with MOQ and capacity, make a profile far more useful for shortlisting.

faqs.question: Should I publish my factory address on the profile?
faqs.answer: Publish the address you are willing to have buyers and inspectors visit. Buyers use it to confirm that the site exists. If you are not ready to publish it, complete the rest of the profile first and add it when the information is settled.

faqs.question: How are claims on my profile shown to buyers?
faqs.answer: The profile shows an evidence level describing how information was confirmed. A claim that is only self-declared is marked as such. It is not presented as independently verified unless there are records to support that.

faqs.question: Can I edit the profile after it is published?
faqs.answer: Yes. Claim an existing profile to maintain certificates, photos and self-assessment information yourself. Keep details current, especially certificate validity and capacity, so buyers are not evaluating outdated information.

h1Question: What Do International Buyers Look for When Choosing Chinese Manufacturers?
blufSummary: International buyers usually evaluate whether a Chinese supplier is legitimate, capable, consistent and low risk before placing an order. They check company identity, manufacturing capability, product quality controls, certificate authenticity, production capacity, delivery capability, communication, export experience and audit readiness. A factory that can show evidence for each of these points is easier to qualify than one that only makes claims.

faqs.question: Do buyers always require a factory audit before ordering?
faqs.answer: Not always. For a first small order, a buyer may rely on verification and document checks. For larger or recurring orders, many buyers request an independent factory audit. The audit scope depends on the product, industry and standard the buyer uses.

faqs.question: Does a high score or complete profile mean a factory is audited?
faqs.answer: No. Profile completeness and self-assessment scores are not audit results. Only a factory audit records what was found on site. The profile distinguishes these with an evidence level so buyers do not mistake self-declared information for an independent assessment.

faqs.question: How should a factory prepare for buyer questions about quality?
faqs.answer: Keep records of incoming material checks, in-process inspections and final inspection results, and show how corrective actions are closed. Buyers value a working process with records over a general statement that quality is important.

faqs.question: What can a factory do if it has no export experience yet?
faqs.answer: State the capability accurately, show real production evidence, and complete the profile with certificates and factory photos. Buyers accept new exporters when the basic facts are clear and verifiable, even if the market list is short.
